topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the final lecture of the course, outlining its core aims regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the primary conventional treatment modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents—alongside the challenges of systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific defects and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and overcoming resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule inhibitors against oncogenic kinases and examine the molecular mechanisms driving drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail therapeutic approaches that use engineered antibodies to target cell-surface tumor antigens, either directly or linked to cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for anti-tumor immune surveillance and describe immunotherapies that harness or engineer T cells, including checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the overarching challenges in oncology, historical improvements in patient survival, emerging therapeutic directions, and ethical considerations in treatment design.
